_comment: Content assertions for the lookup-recipe-smoke workflow. The URL-liveness pass confirms each lookup-recipe target still resolves (200); these assertions confirm the fetched file still contains the symbols the skills actually depend on. A renamed or removed upstream symbol would pass a 200-only check but break the recipe semantically - this catches that. Matching is fixed-string (grep -F), case-sensitive. Add an entry (or a symbol) whenever a recipe or concept starts leaning on a new upstream symbol; drop one when a recipe stops referencing it.

assertions.why: The contracts/review skills teach the four-verb ACL taxonomy (allow / allowThis / allowTransient / allowPublic), the branchless FHE.select pattern, the on-chain verifyDecryptResult decrypt flow, and narrowing casts (asEuint8). FHE.decrypt is the removed legacy synchronous initiator - if it reappears, the deprecated-symbols guidance needs review.
The SDK error-handling concept enumerates err.code off the CofheErrorCode union and catches CofheError; both are the anchors the recipe greps for.
The SDK init recipe and encrypted-input cast lean on these top-level exports.
The permit-lifecycle and sharing-permit concepts reference the permit utilities and the sealing-key surface exported here.
The fhenix-tests recipe tells Claude to look for exactly these helpers on the CoFheTest base your test inherits.
ACL runtime semantics back the user-facing FHE.allow* wrappers; the recipe resolves this file by name (path has moved before), so confirm the contract still lives here.
TaskManager holds the runtime ACL / handle-lifecycle logic the recipe points at; same name-resolution caveat as ACL.sol.
